name: Phosphorus Deficiency
description: Phosphorus is critical for energy transfer (ATP), root development, and flowering. Deficiency causes stunted growth, delayed maturity, and purple discoloration in many crops.
symptoms: Dark green or bluish-green leaves with purple or red pigmentation
Stunted growth and reduced tillering in cereals
causes: Highly acidic or alkaline soils (pH <5.5 or >7.5) locking up phosphorus
High aluminum or iron content in tropical soils fixing phosphorus
Cold or waterlogged soils reducing root activity
treatments: Apply phosphorus fertilizer (single superphosphate, triple superphosphate, DAP)
Use rock phosphate on acidic soils
Apply organic manure or compost to increase phosphorus availability
Foliar spray of mono-ammonium phosphate (MAP) solution
prevention: Conduct soil testing and maintain optimal pH (6.0-6.5)
Apply phosphorus based on soil test recommendations
Incorporate organic matter to improve phosphorus availability
Use mycorrhizal inoculants to enhance phosphorus uptake
Band-apply phosphorus near the root zone for efficiency
